paragraphs: Swamiji liked to share an old tale about a king and a fortune-teller. One day an astrologer arrived at the royal court with grim news: by his reckoning, the king had only six months left to live.

The king went pale. Fear gripped him so tightly that he seemed ready to collapse on the spot. His minister, a sharp and sensible man, tried to calm him, insisting that such astrologers were nothing but fools. But the terrified king refused to listen.

Seeing that words would not work, the minister came up with a plan. He summoned the astrologer back to the palace and asked whether he was certain of his calculations. The astrologer replied that there was no room for error, but, to be thorough, he worked through every figure once more. Again he declared them perfectly right. The king's face turned ashen.
Then the minister turned to the astrologer with a simple question: when did he expect his own death? "In twelve years," came the confident answer.

In a flash the minister drew his sword and struck the man down. Turning to the king, he pointed out that the liar who had foretold twelve more years for himself had not survived even a moment. The prophecy that had frozen the king with terror was exposed as empty.
learn: Fear often grows from predictions and rumours we never stop to test. Before letting a forecast about your future, a horoscope, a bad mock result, a harsh comment, crush you, question it. Strength means facing what scares you with a clear head.
